c.tagline: Cyberpunk mountain metropolis of fog, hot pot, and cities stacked along the Yangtze.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are standard with a starting fare around 10 yuan; many drivers prefer cash or a WeChat/Alipay QR code, and few speak English, so have your destination written in Chinese.

emergency.note: 110 connects to police, 120 for ambulance, and 119 for fire. English support is limited, so use a translation app or ask hotel staff to help place the call.

hood_landmark.Nanshan (Nan'an): Nanshan One Tree Viewing Platform, Chongqing

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the crowded Jiefangbei and Hongyadong areas and on packed metro lines, and skip unlicensed taxis at stations.

hood_desc: The dense downtown peninsula between the Yangtze and Jialing rivers, centered on the Jiefangbei (Liberation Monument) pedestrian mall and the stacked Hongyadong stilt houses; best for first-timers who want everything within walking distance.

A major commercial and nightlife hub on the north bank across the Jialing, packed with malls, bars, and restaurants and adjacent to the gleaming Jiangbeizui financial district; ideal for shopping and going out.
A forested mountain on the south bank famous for its cluster of hot pot restaurants, the One Tree lookout, and sweeping night views of the illuminated skyline; quieter, greener, and scenic.
A lively university and youth district around Sanxia Square and the Testbed2 creative park, with cheap eats, indie shops, and quick access to Ciqikou; affordable and full of student energy.
A 1,000-year-old riverside porcelain town of cobbled lanes, teahouses, and street-food stalls near the Jialing River; touristy but atmospheric, best for old-town wandering and souvenirs.

water.note: Tap water is treated for household use but not recommended for drinking; use bottled water.

transit.hours: Trains run roughly 6:30 AM to 10:30-11:00 PM depending on the line.
transit.note: Chongqing Rail Transit is an extensive metro network famous for its straddle-beam monorail Lines 2 and 3 — Line 2 threads directly through the Liziba station built into a residential tower, and the system climbs the mountainous terrain with dramatic elevation changes, bridges, and cliffside stations.
transit.pay: Pay by QR code through Alipay/WeChat or the Yu Kuai Xing app, a rechargeable Chang'an Tong transit card, or single-journey tokens from station machines (fares run ~2-10 yuan by distance).

bus: Long-distance coaches from Chongqing Coach Station and Longtousi Bus Station

car.idp: Not valid — China does not recognize the IDP; visitors need a temporary Chinese licence, so most do not self-drive

ferry: Yangtze River cross-river passenger ferries and cruise piers at Chaotianmen
train: Chongqingbei (North), Chongqingxi (West) & Shapingba high-speed rail stations
High-speed links to Chengdu, Xi'an, Wuhan, Guiyang and beyond

transit.m: Rail Transit Line 3/10 to city center (~45-60 min)
Taxi to Jiefangbei city center (40-55 min)
Airport shuttle bus to downtown (~50 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected or practiced in restaurants, taxis, or hotels; a service charge is occasionally added at upscale venues.

landmarks: Hongya Cave (Hongyadong)
A dazzling stilt-house complex stacked eleven stories up a cliffside, glowing gold against the Jialing River at night for one of China's most photographed skylines.
Liziba Monorail Station
The famous spot where a monorail train appears to burst directly through the middle of a residential apartment building, epitomizing Chongqing's vertical, mountain-city chaos.
Chongqing People's Great Hall (Renmin Dahuitang)
A monumental Ming-style domed auditorium modeled after the Temple of Heaven, standing as the city's grandest piece of civic architecture.
Eling Park
A hilltop garden offering panoramic views over the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers and the dense high-rise skyline.
Ciqikou Ancient Town
A well-preserved Ming and Qing-era riverside town of stone lanes, teahouses, and traditional architecture that feels like a step back in time.
Chaotianmen Square and Raffles City Chongqing
The dramatic point where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet, now framed by the sail-shaped towers of Raffles City and its sky bridge.
Dazu Rock Carvings
A UNESCO World Heritage site of exquisite Buddhist, Taoist, and Confucian rock carvings dating back over a thousand years, set in the hills outside the city.
Nanshan Yizhi Botanical Garden (One Tree Viewing Platform)
A hillside overlook renowned as the best vantage point for a sweeping night view of Chongqing's glittering downtown skyline.
Jiefangbei CBD Pedestrian Street
The neon-lit commercial heart of Chongqing centered on the Liberation Monument, a bustling hub of shopping, skyscrapers, and street life.
Guanyinqiao
A vibrant, ultra-modern commercial district famed for its towering LED billboards and dense cluster of skyscrapers illuminated after dark.

train.note: Chongqing has no international passenger trains; the Chongqing-Duisburg rail link is a freight service. Chongqing North is the main station, with high-speed G-trains to Chengdu in about 1.5 hours and Beijing in around 12 hours - note that the fast trains use the North Square while slower K and T services use the South Square, and the two are a long walk apart. Chongqing West is the newer high-speed station, connected to metro Line 5, while the original Chongqing (Caiyuanba) station has been closed for redevelopment. The longest single run in China, 3,535 km from Harbin in about 48 hours, terminates here.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Chongqing. The main terminals are Chongqing Long-Distance Bus Station next to the old railway station, Chenjiaping station for destinations west, and the South Plaza terminal at Chongqing North; buses run hourly to Chengdu (about 2.5 hours), Nanchong and Xi'an, and cover the Wulong and Dazu areas. Tickets are bought at the counters or on Chinese travel apps.

intl.to: Yichang (China) - Three Gorges cruise downstream on the Yangtze

ferry.note: Chongqing is the standard starting point for Yangtze cruises through the Three Gorges to Yichang, taking three to four nights downstream and four to five upstream, with fares from around ¥700 to ¥2,500 depending on the ship. Most international-standard cruises now board at the Chongqing Cruise Home Port at Guojiatuo, well downstream of the city, rather than at central Chaotianmen - confirm your pier when you book, as the transfer takes an hour or more. Cabins sell out in spring and autumn, and the scheduled point-to-point passenger boats that once ran the river have largely been replaced by these cruise ships.

half.name: Zhongshan Ancient Town
half.blurb: A well-preserved Ming-and-Qing-era river town of stone streets and old shopfronts along the Longxi River.

half.name: Laitan Ancient Town
half.blurb: A riverside town of over a thousand years, with old wooden buildings, a stone bridge and a laid-back teahouse scene.

half.name: Jinyun Mountain
half.blurb: A forested mountain reserve with ancient temples and cable-car views over the river valley outside the city.

full.name: Wulong Karst National Geopark
full.blurb: A UNESCO site of giant sinkholes, natural stone bridges and cave systems carved into dramatic karst limestone terrain.

full.name: Fengdu Ghost City
full.blurb: A hillside complex of temples and statues themed around Chinese folklore's underworld, overlooking the Yangtze River.
